content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge is deciding a collision between the defender's and challenger's chain readings, so rule K-C governs how that collision must be weighed.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse — reading one: compare the whole chain's footing; reading two: decide by whether a singled verse names the channel.","why":"The judge treats Acts 2:30's silence about whose body is the channel as leaving the link open, which is the retired verse-by-verse/stating-verse inquiry rather than the required chain-against-chain weighing by footing."}
